# Messages posted to the host and what it answers (docs/requests.md): byte
# for byte, every binding reproduces them (README.md). Run by the suite's
# runner.
#
# A case is a line "request <name>", then:
#   setup <name>      the host it runs on (README.md, "Setups"; default empty)
#   send <hex>        a message posted (ta_host_post), as CBOR
#   reply <hex>       its REPLY; "reply none": the post appends no REPLY (a
#                     message without an id)
#   refused           the next send is first refused memory (the host's
#                     allocator refuses every block): TA_ERROR_NO_MEMORY,
#                     nothing applied and no REPLY; then sent again: the reply
#   event <name> <n>  the event <name>, without data, for session <n>
#   run               the host runs until idle (host.run); the notification
#                     lines after it are its NOTIFICATIONs, in order (none
#                     when there are none)
#   notification <hex> a NOTIFICATION of the run before it
#   diag <text>       the hex line before it, in diagnostic notation
#   only reference    a case no binding's API makes: run by the reference
#                     (ta-conform) alone; a binding skips it (README.md,
#                     "Reference-only cases")
# A case's lines go in order to one host. In a reply, 39999("<type>") is a
# wildcard (README.md); an error's message always is one.

request not CBOR
only reference
send ff
diag (not CBOR)

diag {"id":null,"error":{"code":-32700,"message":39999("text"),"data":{"reason":"malformed","path":""}}}
